clue.text: Six-footers are examined in his study

definitions.text: Six-footers are examined in his study

parts.words: Six-footers are examined in his study
parts.note: six-footers are not tall people but creatures with six legs, i.e. insects, which this scientist studies

explanation.surface: Tall men are inspected in some scholar's private room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Six-footers' suggests tall people; insects have six feet, so the person studying them is the scientist of insects.
explanation.definitionFit: A scientist specialising in insects examines six-legged creatures as his field of research.

clue.text: Former wife pretended, to be without shelter

parts.note: an ex is a former wife or partner
posed means pretended, as in posed as a doctor

explanation.surface: An ex-wife who put on an act was left out in the cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Being open to the elements and unprotected is being without shelter.

clue.text: Start ninth year, say, with three leaflets

indicators.note: say signals that the phrase is spoken, its sound giving the botanical word

parts.note: you begin your ninth year of life on turning eight, so the phrase means turn eight

explanation.surface: A plant starts its ninth season, with leaves in threes.
explanation.walkthrough: On your eighth birthday you start your ninth year: you turn eight, which spoken gives the botanical term.
explanation.definitionFit: In botany a ternate leaf is one divided into three leaflets, like clover.

clue.text: It provided illumination for Lorenzo's bank (Mer, of Venice)

definitions.text: It provided illumination for Lorenzo's bank (Mer, of Venice)

parts.words: It provided illumination for Lorenzo's bank (Mer, of Venice)
parts.note: in The Merchant of Venice Lorenzo says how sweet the light of the night sky sleeps upon this bank; a bank of earth, not money

explanation.definitionFit: Lorenzo's line in Shakespeare praises the soft night light from the sky falling on a grassy bank.

clue.text: See copper married by, this surrogate

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning see or behold
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: Look, a policeman got married to this stand-in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' suggests a policeman, but it is the metal, symbol Cu.
explanation.definitionFit: A locum is a doctor or cleric standing in temporarily for another, a substitute.

clue.text: Admission of a theologian made Galen rejoice

indicators.note: admission of means letting the theologian in, so he goes inside the rearranged name
made means the letters of the name are reworked into a new form

parts.note: DD is Doctor of Divinity, a theologian

explanation.surface: Letting a churchman in made the Greek physician Galen happy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made' rearranges GALEN into GLAEN, and 'Admission of' lets DD (Doctor of Divinity) in after GLA.
explanation.definitionFit: To gladden is to make happy or cheer, transitively bringing joy.

clue.text: Form of address two commanders found a blow?

parts.note: sir is a respectful form of address
OC is officer commanding, the first of the two commanders
CO is commanding officer, the second of the two

explanation.surface: A polite greeting from two officers turns out to be a punch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a blow' is not a punch but a wind blowing; the two commanders are OC (officer commanding) and CO (commanding officer), and 'found' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: The sirocco is a hot wind from North Africa, and a wind is something that blows.

clue.text: The more reckless chaps in punt cause confusion

indicators.note: in means the reckless chaps are placed inside the word for punt

parts.note: to punt is to bet, a gamble
wilder means more reckless
chaps are men

explanation.surface: The wilder lads in a flat-bottomed boat cause chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'punt' looks like a boat but is a gamble, BET; 'in' puts WILDER and MEN inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Bewilderment is a state of perplexity, being completely puzzled.

clue.text: Eastern spring right to produce grass

parts.note: a spa is a mineral spring

explanation.surface: A spring in the East gives rise to a crop of grass.
explanation.definitionFit: Esparto is a tough Spanish and North African grass used for making rope and paper.

clue.text: Fish assumes angry colour, being burnt

parts.note: the char is a fish of the trout family
red is the colour of anger, as in seeing red

explanation.surface: A fish turns red with rage while being cooked too long.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assumes' is just a joining word: the fish puts on the angry colour, one after the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Scorched or blackened by fire is what burnt food is.

clue.text: Devil, saint, turncoat, or just one airing a grievance?

parts.note: a demon is a devil
a rat is a deserter, one who changes sides

explanation.surface: Is he a devil, a saint, a traitor, or just someone protesting?
explanation.definitionFit: A protester at a rally publicly voices complaints, so is one airing a grievance.

clue.text: Place for theatre-goer?

parts.note: read as two words, a theatre-goer sits in a stall, the ground-floor seats; as one word it means to put in position

explanation.definitionFit: To install is to set something in position, and a theatre-goer is seated in the stalls.

clue.text: Trendy teenager — one with a small portion

parts.note: a Mod was a fashionable 1960s British youth, scooter-riding and smartly dressed
I is the Roman numeral for one
cum is Latin for with, as in a bedroom-cum-study

explanation.surface: A fashionable youngster is one who gets only a little helping.
explanation.walkthrough: A Mod was a stylish British teenager of the 1960s, rival to the Rockers.
explanation.definitionFit: A modicum is a tiny amount, a little bit of something.

clue.text: An artful ruse to sidestep

explanation.surface: A cunning trick lets one step aside.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun it is a cunning trick; as a verb it means to swerve aside to avoid something.

clue.text: Coloured cape for a raw recruit

parts.note: green is a colour, so coloured can stand for it
Horn, as in Cape Horn at the tip of South America, is a famous cape

explanation.surface: A newly enlisted soldier is issued with a dyed cloak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cape' looks like a cloak, but it is a headland: Cape Horn.
explanation.definitionFit: A novice or inexperienced newcomer is called green, and the full word means a raw beginner.

clue.text: Cried out, having got right into. River Dee we hear

indicators.note: into means the word for right goes inside the river's name

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, England
a claim is a right to something

indicators.note: we hear signals that the river's name is taken by its sound, a single letter

parts.note: the river Dee is pronounced like the letter D

explanation.surface: Someone yelled after wading right into the River Dee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' puts CLAIM inside EXE (a Devon river); 'we hear' turns Dee into the letter D. 'having got' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: To exclaim is to call out suddenly, so the past tense means shouted.

clue.text: Article is curious but practical

indicators.note: curious means odd or strange, so the letters before it are put into an odd new order

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece is peculiar yet sensible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curious' signals rearranging the letters of ARTICLE and IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Being realistic means taking a sensible, down-to-earth view of what can be done.

clue.text: The mode set by leaving Libya in plenty of time?

indicators.note: in means the shortened country goes inside the long stretch of time

parts.note: an aeon is an immensely long time

indicators.note: leaving means the word by departs from the country's name

explanation.surface: Music set a long time ago by someone who has left Libya.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' takes BY out of LIBYA to leave LIA, and 'in' puts that inside AEON.
explanation.definitionFit: Aeolian is one of the church modes in music, the scale running A to A on white notes.

clue.text: Stimulate one new feature of church architecture

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a spire is a tapering steeple on a church

explanation.surface: Arouse interest in a novel element of church design.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspire is to rouse or encourage someone to act or create.

clue.text: Doctor a short distance from these soldiers

parts.note: a foot is a short distance, abbreviated ft

explanation.surface: A medic is stationed a little way from a group of troops.
explanation.walkthrough: A draft is a detachment of soldiers sent off for some duty.
explanation.definitionFit: A detachment of troops selected for special duty is called a draft.

clue.text: Refuse to be carried away by this public servant.

definitions.text: Refuse to be carried away by this public servant.

parts.words: Refuse to be carried away by this public servant.
parts.note: refuse is the noun rubbish, not the verb decline; the council worker collects it from homes

explanation.definitionFit: A British council worker collects household rubbish, so refuse is taken away by him.

clue.text: Adapt a stove, by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it signals the phrase is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a range is a cooking stove, so a stove is a range

explanation.surface: Modify a cooker, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: A range is a large cooking stove; 'a range' said quickly sounds like the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrange music is to adapt it for different instruments or voices.

clue.text: For example, musicians discarding ex-pupil — they're so self-centred

parts.note: e.g. abbreviates exempli gratia, for example

indicators.note: discarding means the musicians throw away the letters for the former pupil

parts.note: oboists are musicians who play the oboe
OB stands for old boy, a former pupil of a school

explanation.surface: Musicians, for example, who throw out a former schoolmate are terribly vain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discarding' removes OB (old boy, a British term for a former pupil) from OBOISTS, leaving OISTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-centred people think chiefly of themselves, which is what conceited, selfish types do.

clue.text: Loves somehow to complete the puzzle

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters are arranged in some other way

explanation.surface: Somehow, a lover manages to finish the crossword.
explanation.definitionFit: To solve a crossword is to finish it by finding every answer.

clue.text: Her tours are outside America, of course

definitions.text: Her tours are outside America, of course

parts.words: Her tours are outside America, of course
parts.note: a country spoken of as she, whose travels are naturally abroad from America, being a European land often confused by Americans with a southern one

explanation.surface: A woman's trips are naturally all abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: This European country is, of course, not in America.

clue.text: Virgin Islands in experiment of little importance

indicators.note: in means the abbreviations are placed inside the word for experiment

parts.note: a trial is an experiment or test
V is an abbreviation for virgin
I is an abbreviation for island or islands

explanation.surface: The Virgin Islands are the subject of a minor experiment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts V and I inside TRIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something trivial is petty and insignificant, hardly worth bothering about.

clue.text: Fellows inside paid nothing for this souvenir

indicators.note: inside means the fellows go within the word for paid

parts.note: to meet a bill is to pay it, so met means paid
fellows are men
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Some chaps who got in free kept this as a keepsake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' puts MEN within MET, paid as in met the cost; O for nothing follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A memento is a keepsake kept to remember something by, much as a souvenir is.

clue.text: Seat of Missouri's autonomy, presumably

parts.note: a city in Missouri, seat of Jackson County, whose name suggests self-rule; seat is a county seat, not a chair

explanation.definitionFit: The city in Missouri bears a name meaning self-government, so jokingly it would be the seat of the state's autonomy.
